assertions.value: The authors report that the average approximation ratio of the original MaxCut problems is 0.75, while the decomposed graphs average 0.96 for both Gurobi and QAOA.

assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on twenty-five random 100-vertex 3-regular graphs (Sec. IV).

assertions.value: The authors report that the reduced problems need approximately 1/10 of the vertices of the original instances, and that they measured optimal solutions for ten 100-vertex graphs with single-layer QAOA on the Quantinuum H1-1, sampling each circuit 500 times.
quotes: On average, the reduced problems require only approximately 1/10 of the number of vertices than the original MaxCut instances.
we are able to measure optimal solutions for ten 100-vertex graphs by running single-layer QAOA circuits on the Quantinuum trapped-ion quantum computer H1-1, sampling each circuit only 500 times.
assertions.certainty_reason: Own simulation and hardware runs, Sec. IV.

papers.title_in_file: Bridging Quantum Chemistry and MaxCut: Classical Performance Guarantees and Quantum Algorithms for the Hartree-Fock Method
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sec. III B MaxCut background, Sec. IV results, Sec. V Conclusion; appendices not read

assertions.value: The authors state that the MaxCut reformulation of SCF provides performance guarantees at each SCF step, irrespective of the complexity of the optimization landscape.

assertions.certainty_reason: Derivation uses the Goemans-Williamson MaxCut guarantee; the reader did not verify the derivation, so the coordinator should grade it.

assertions.value: The authors report, from classical-hardware calculations on OH- and N2 with up to 220 qubits (spin-orbitals), that MaxCut-SCF and QUBO-SCF are competitive with conventional Hartree-Fock solvers and resist internal instabilities.

quotes: The largest problem addressed in this study involves a system comprised of 220 qubits (equivalently, spin-orbitals).
